# **Multimodal modelling of human emotion using sound, image and text** **fusion**
**Seyed Sadegh Hosseini** **[1]** **· Mohammad Reza Yamaghani** **[2]** **· Soodabeh Poorzaker Arabani** **[2]**

Received: 26 May 2023 / Revised: 2 July 2023 / Accepted: 14 July 2023 / Published online: 11 August 2023 © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag London Ltd., part of Springer Nature 2023

Multimodal emotion recognition and analysis are considered as an evolving field of research. The improvement of the multimodal fusion mechanism plays an important role in the more detailed recognition of the recognised emotion. The performance of the emotion recognition system was optimised, and a model for multimodal emotion recognition from audio, text and video data was proposed. First, the data were fused as a combination of video and audio, then as a combination of audio and text as binary, and finally the results were fused together. The final output included audio, text and video data, taking into account common features. The convolutional neural network and long-term and short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) were then used to extract audio. Next, the Inception-Res Net-v2 network was used to extract facial expressions from the video. The output fused data were used by LSTM as the input of the Softmax classifier to recognise the emotion of audio and video features fusion. In addition, the CNN-LSTM was combined in the form of a binary channel for learning audio emotion features. Meanwhile, a Bi-LSTM network was used to extract the text features and Softmax was used to classify the fused features. Finally, the generated results were fused together for the final classification, and the logistic regression model was used for fusion and classification. As the results showed, the recognition accuracy of the proposed method on the IEMOCAP dataset was 82.9%.

Multimodal emotion recognition studies have made good progress using effective fusion of unimodal information such as audio, face and text. Extracted features from other modes such as audio and text can be combined due to the internal correlation of different modes to obtain an efficient emotional feature for emotion recognition. It is possible to use deep neural network model to learn features in multivariate data. It is possible to transform the original high-dimensional heterogeneous data into a nonlinear mode in the same feature space for several times and then used to extract and select multimodal features.

We propose a method that, like the structure of the human brain, selects the results derived from audio, text and image processing by selecting common and effective features for understanding the real emotion. In this context, we need a model capable of extracting effective features in a different way from existing algorithms. This paper presents a method for extracting effective features in audio and text, and a method for extracting effective features in audio and images. After extraction, the results of these two methods are merged through data fusion and used as input for the classifier.

chunks.raw_text: network are combined into a CNN-LSTM network and an LSTM layer is added. To transform the input data from the convolution layer and then for re-learning, we input the data into the LSTM layer. The correlation part consists of a maximum aggregation layer and two convolutional layers. The convolution layer has similar parameters to the CNN network parameters and a linear unit (ReLU) is used in the activation function [23]. The output of a set of CNNs feeds directly into LSTMs in the shared CNN-LSTM network. In this way, the advanced information including long-term contextual and local information dependencies can be obtained. However, CNNs leave a lot of data and focus on local information. A method using CNN and Bi-LSTM channels was presented to prevent the loss of valuable data. A set of four one-dimensional convolutional layers were used in the CNN channel with different numbers of filters for 1-D temporal input (audio features). In addition, the maximum pooling and general average pooling layers were applied to perform the average pooling and maximum pooling operations on the data. A set of Bi-LSTM cells with 256 arguments was placed in the Bi-LSTM channel to extract the information of long-term textual dependencies, and an attention mechanism was used to find more effective features. Finally, the data from the two channels were combined and the output was placed in a dense layer. After inducing the nonlinear change, the correlation of these features was determined and mapped to the output space [24] (Fig. 3).

chunks.raw_text: **Face feature extraction** The amount of video data is usually very large. Therefore, we need to determine the face contour in each frame of the video and reduce the size of the frame image through face contour cropping, which is necessary for processing the data and obtaining the next features [25]. Here, the emotional information of the videos is determined by short-term feature extraction using InceptionRes Net-v2 network and signal Fourier transform (STFT) for deep feature extraction. The STFT is an audio signal processing tool that provides a very useful class of time–frequency distributions by specifying the signal amplitude that varies with frequency and time. Inception-Res Net-v2 refers to a CNN developed by Google in 2016 by representing the ResNet network based on the Inception model, which has an accurate diagnostic effect on objects with high similarity. The network is considered a prototype of Inception V3, which uses the idea of connectivity in the Microsoft ResNet model, where the neural network receives deeper training. It is possible to significantly simplify the Inception module by using multiple 3 × 3 convolutions instead of 5 × 5 and 7 × 7 convolutions. As a result, the computational complexity and the dimensions of the parameters are significantly reduced and the training rate of the network is increased. The algorithm has a higher spatial complexity compared to other networks.

chunks.raw_text: Mital et al. [30] proposed multimodal multiplicative emotion recognition (M3ER): first, feature vectors were extracted from three raw methods. Then, these features are fed to the model evaluation step to obtain the effective and ineffective features, and the former are used to build the proxy feature vectors. Finally, by fusing the selected features, they are used to determine the six emotions using the fusion of the final feature level with the attention module. The recognition accuracy of M3ER in IEMOCAP was 82.7%. The results showed that the recognition accuracy of the presented multimodal model outperformed the unimodal model and other multimodal models in the dataset.

chunks.raw_text: A multimodal emotion recognition model was presented using audio, video and text from the IEMOCAP database. First, LSTM and two-channel CNN were used to determine the acoustic emotion features. Then, Bi-LSTM was used to extract the text features. Finally, a DNN was used to learn the fusion features. The model used deep learning networks, artificial and advanced features and took into account time and textual information in the data. L2 adaptation was also used to optimise the model. An (A/V) bimodal fusion was simultaneously used through deep learning using Long/Short-Term Memory Convolutional Neural Network andInception-ResNet-v2forextractingfacialexpressionfeatures in audio and video. In addition, the obtained features were fed into the LSTM unit and the individual methods were linked together to extract the fusion features using feature selection of chi-square test. The output feature data from the LSTM were then fed into the Softmax emotion recognition classifier. The results on the IEMOCAP dataset showed that
